messages:
maria: CI failure on PR #21073 microbench (batching/timer test). seeing ~12% tail perf regression vs main. link: https://ci.internal/reports/21073
perf-bot: [auto] benchmark: microbench/batcher_timer  - threshold diff +12.4% (regression). artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/21073/bench.html
jon: can you paste the raw bench output and the env used in CI? is this reproducible locally?
maria: raw snippet: ```
Benchmark: microbench/batcher_timer
Env: ubuntu-20.04, cuda 12.1, driver 535.113
Result (main): p50=6.8ms p95=28.1ms
Result (PR #21073): p50=7.6ms p95=32.1ms
Delta: +12.4% p50, +14.2% p95
```
maria: repro steps used in CI runner: ```
docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ 
  -v $PWD:/work -w /work redwood/bench:latest \ 
  ./run_microbench --model=gpt-small --iters=1000 --batcher-timer=8ms
```
kevin: repro'd on my A100 (driver 535.113) with same docker image. Not repro on my dev 3090 (driver 525.x). so looks driver/GPU specific. I instrumented kv cache metrics: kv_hit_rate dropped from 0.84 -> 0.68 under PR edges for short seq workloads.
sophie: posted flamegraph + kernel trace: ```
flamegraph summary:
  matmul_kernel_v2  (hot)  42%  <-- new selector picks this for small batches
  batch_coalescer   18%
  kv_cache_lookup   12%
  overhead/dispatch 10%
note: old runs pick matmul_kernel_v1 which spends less time in shared mem sync
```
dave: quick history: two commits in the PR set: commit abc12345 changed batcher timer default from 4ms -> 8ms (intended to reduce syscalls), commit def67890 modified kernel selector heuristics to prefer matmul_kernel_v2 when batch_size <= 8 (perf tweak). suspect interaction with driver 535 heuristic.
jon: can we bisect which change is culprit? I can try locally.
jon: bisect result: reverted def67890 (kernel selector) -> perf returns to baseline. reverted abc12345 (timer) -> still regression. so kernel selector tweak is the immediate cause.
maria: thanks, that matches Sophie profile. So root cause: selector prefers matmul_kernel_v2 which on 535 driver/A100 increases shared-mem stall leading to higher latency and lower kv hit ratio due to longer scheduling windows.
kevin: plan: revert kernel selector tweak in the PR (small revert in same PR to unblock CI), keep timer change in for follow-up. I'll open PR revert: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/21073/revert-kernel-selector
kevin: /cc @maria @jon please review quickly, I will push if no objections in 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ci-bot: CI status: revert PR started, running microbench suite. artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/21073/revert-run.html
maria: once revert merges, plan to run extended canary on Dedicated pool (region eu-west) with driver 535 to validate. if stable we'll ship.
dave: long-term: we need to add a driver/gpu-aware kernel preference matrix in the kernel selector service and add a small smoke test in CI that runs microbench on one A100 image with driver 535 to catch regressions like this.
jon: agree. also adding a perf unit test to cover short-batch matmul path. opened issue #4521.
kevin: reverted and merged, CI green on microbench in revert-run. :tada:
perf-bot: [auto] benchmark: microbench/batcher_timer - revert-run diff -0.3% (within noise).
maria: final: revert unblocks rollout. follow-up tickets: #4521 (selector matrix), #4522 (A100-535 smoke CI), #4523 (investigate kv cache scheduling interplay).
kevin: :thumbsup: will follow up on selector matrix prototype this week.
